content:
building on #announcements > Release candidate: Roc 0.1.0-RC1 we now have an 0.1.0-RC2 release candidate published!

The commit is ee835686f9eae076bee7422c26e7cf8deb20aa0e - nearly the same commit as RC1, except with a fix for a roc check hang cherry-picked onto it because it was blocking a project and couldn't be worked around.

I am being intentionally conservative about the RC process because I want to avoid accidentally introducing regressions. (There have been a bunch of performance improvements and bugfixes landed on main which I am intentionally leaving out of RC2 to avoid the chance of regressions. There will be an 0.1.1 with them released after 0.1.0, hopefully within a couple of weeks!)

My default plan is to promote 0.1.0-RC2 to 0.1.0 in the next few days, and announce on Monday. (I'll share a draft of the announcement post here for feedback when it's ready, but I have to finish writing the draft first!) So if there are any bugs on RC2 that you can't work around, this will be the last chance to bring them up! :smile:

I updated my project to RC2 and didn't encounter any bugs.
Looking forward to reading the draft! :smile:
All my checks are :check:
My projects that passed on RC1 are passing on RC2 :thumbs_up: The only bug I've found since RC1 (https://github.com/roc-lang/roc/issues/13510) can be worked around.
Rocco and it's packages are now on RC2 as well. No issues.

Claude and I ran RC2 over 39,000 lines of Roc in 68 files (a JavaScript interpreter, an x86-64 compiler, and a book builder). It passed our full gate, and every executable it built, the compiler included, was byte-for-byte identical to RC1's.
BoxingKangaroos.roc (140 lines including comments, empty lines, and tests) also compiles byte identically on RC2. (along with the rest of the Rocco-based app)

My networking project is failing tests that passed on a previous nightly, still tracking it down with an LLM but its pointing to opt=speed as the thing that's breaking the example, which is here: https://gitlab.com/ddombrow/roc-net/-/blob/d2220629a1f82e6c3d43ede9f1d3d2d347a8d054/tests/specialization_bug/main.roc.

It's more-or-less ruled out my platform as the problem but not %100 sure I trust that of course. Still running that down.

https://gitlab.com/ddombrow/roc-net/-/merge_requests/10

Edit: I guess the most relevant thing to mention is that this passes tests with --opt=dev, --opt=size and --specialize=no, but fails with no options as --opt=speed is default I think...
Try --opt=size, Im using that in some places as a workaround

Yeah opt=size works. I had the llm create a test platform standalone to help isolate:
https://github.com/ddombrow/roc-net/tree/105d281dcd26a9f1765e697235cb0bb8afb99646/tests/specialization_bug/standalone
Yeah were tracking bugs like this, it might be fixed already in the nightlies, but unless its a complete blocker with no workaround, probably not worth delaying the release.
yep no worries not blocking me, I'll check to see if the next releases fix it
